thread:
olivia: quick proposal — can we switch default LLM request/response logs to minimal mode? idea is: keep request id, model, user_id (hashed), error flags, and store hashed prompt/response only when needed. removes full bodies from standard logs. cc @sheila_sec @ben

devon: curious — what does 'when needed' look like? who can unhash? we often need full text to reproduce customer issues.

olivia: good q. plan is: by default no full bodies. sampling for reproductions via a gated workflow: 1) developer opens access request with justification 2) security approves 3) short-lived unhash token issued 4) audit trail. most debug will rely on deterministic hashes + repro inputs we can request from customer.

ben: hmm ok. also need to consider embeddings/derived artifacts — those are PII in some flows. we should avoid saving those unless explicitly requested.

olivia: agree. proposal also suggests storing a salted HMAC of prompt/response (sha256) + salt id, rather than reversible encryption. only KMS-backed mapping for approved tickets.

sheila_sec: high level — sounds reasonable. a few constraints: 1) salt must be rotated quarterly and stored in KMS, 2) mapping between hash and plaintext must never be stored in the same system as logs, 3) access must require JIRA ticket and 2nd approver for PROD, 4) ephemeral unmasked payloads must expire and be deleted automatically. also add a privacy review for embeddings handling.

alex_sre: traffic note — if we hash every token payload at ingest we'll add CPU. propose we sample 1% for full capture for high-volume routes and keep hashing for the rest. we should also ensure batching doesn't change hash semantics.

olivia: good call. intended default is no per-token hashing in hot path — compute hash at the message-level only (prompt_text -> HMAC). will add sampling config.

devon: can you drop a config snippet so infra can eyeball?

olivia: sure — rough example:
```yaml
logging:
  llm_payloads:
    mode: minimal  # options: full | minimal | off
    minimal_fields: [request_id, model, prompt_hash, response_hash, error]
    hash_algorithm: HMAC-SHA256
    salt_id_header: X-Hash-Salt-Id
    full_capture_policy:
      enabled: true
      sample_rate: 0.01
      approval_required: true
    retention_days: 30
```

sheila_sec: add: require salt_id header to be present for any full capture requests and a ticket ref in metadata. Also document the threat model in the RFC (insider access, rogue unmask attempts).

ben: one more — telemetry & billing pipelines read these logs. pls ensure downstream consumers can't access raw via cloud storage. we need IAM filters and column-level masking on export.

olivia: noted. I'll include IAM recommendations and a list of downstream consumers in the RFC/PR.

deploy-bot: Created issue INF-4321: "LLM payload minimality + gated unmask workflow" and linked to drafts/rfc in /docs/rfcs/INF-4321.md

olivia: thanks. I'll push RFC and a small infra PR for a config toggle. tagging @alex_sre for sampling defaults.

alex_sre: will review sampling numbers. for prod routes suggest 0.5% for now until we measure.

devon: ack. please include a short playbook for SRE to request unmasked payloads during incidents.

sheila_sec: and include a checklist for privacy sign-off before enabling any full capture for a customer.

olivia: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
